property_summary: For any caller, after a successful transferOwnership(newOwner) call, the owner must be newOwner; the bug allows any caller to change the owner, violating the invariant when the caller is not the current owner.

After a failed transferOwnership call (tx reverted) the owner must remain unchanged; the bug allows unauthorized callers to change the owner, so a call that would revert on the reference may succeed and change owner.

After the current owner calls transferOwnership, the owner should remain the current owner (since newOwner is ignored) or change to the new owner in the reference, but the mutant always sets owner to zero, violating correct ownership.

For any current owner and any newOwner address, after the current owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), the owner must become newOwner; the buggy version sets owner to address(0), violating this rule.

For any current owner and any newOwner address, after the current owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), the owner must become newOwner; the buggy version sets owner to address(0), violating this rule.

For any current owner and any newOwner address, after the current owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), c.owner() must equal newOwner; the buggy version sets owner to address(0), violating the rule.
For any caller who is the current owner, after transferOwnership(newOwner) completes, c.owner() must equal newOwner; the buggy version sets owner to address(0), violating the rule.
After transferOwnership, owner must equal the argument passed; the bug leaves owner unchanged.

After a successful transferOwnership call by the current owner, the new owner must be able to call an onlyOwner function (owned), which the reference allows and the bug prevents because owner never changes.

For any caller that is not the owner, calling owned() must revert, while the owner calling owned() must succeed; the mutant always reverts even for the owner, so the owner can never successfully call owned().
The reference contract permits the owner to successfully call owned(); the mutant always reverts, so the owner can never successfully call owned().
